extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and patent professionals interested in automated patent-drafting and patent-focused language models
extracted.subtask_description: Training and evaluating language models to generate patent claims (especially claim 1) using reinforcement learning from human feedback, with experiments on claim length, limiting terms, and domain-specific datasets. Emphasis on making models reflect prosecution signals (granted vs pre-grant) while remaining usable on modest hardware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantability as primary objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the likelihood for a language model to generate patent claims that have a higher chance of being granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the probability of grant (or other prosecution success signals) as the principal optimization target when training and evaluating models; prefer outputs that historical data suggests are more likely to be examined and allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use granted vs pre-grant status as feedback labels
rubrics_metrics.description: The system learns from granted patents and pre-grant applications with different rewards. The status of "granted" and "pre-grant" are perceived as labeled human feedback implicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model training can treat grant-status as an implicit human feedback signal by assigning different rewards to granted vs pre-grant documents; ensure dataset labeling and reward design reflect these distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control claim length to influence scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments demonstrate the model's capability to learn from adjusting claim length ... for narrowing claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit length constraints or length-conditioned prompts/training to steer claim scope; evaluate how shorter vs longer claim formulations affect perceived breadth and grant likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include limiting terms to narrow claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Model can learn from inclusion of limiting terms for narrowing claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage or enforce limiting language (e.g., "wherein", specific numerical/structural limits) when a narrower scope is desired; measure effect on downstream grantability signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on claim ones (independent claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: As proof of concept, the experiments focus on claim ones only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial evaluation and model design may concentrate on independent claim 1 as a representative target; note limitations when generalizing to dependent claims or full specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use domain-specific patent dataset (AI patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training data originates from a patent dataset tailored specifically for artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer domain- or technology-specific corpora (here: AI patents) to improve relevance and model performance for that subject area; be explicit about dataset scope when evaluating outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments follow the 3-stage reinforcement learning from human feedback and demonstrate that generative language models are capable of reflecting the human feedback or intent in patent prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a staged RLHF pipeline (as described in the paper) to iteratively align model outputs with prosecution-intent signals; document stages, reward modeling, and evaluation at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for limited and noisy human feedback in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the available human feedback in patent prosecution are limited and the quality of generated patent text requires improvement...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limitations of supervision available from prosecution records (e.g., sparse explicit labels, noisy signals). Incorporate uncertainty estimates, conservative evaluation, and plans for human-in-the-loop quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware/resource efficiency for usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation utilizes modern techniques that enable execution on a single consumer-grade GPU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design training and inference processes to be resource-efficient so models can be run on modest hardware; document techniques used (quantization, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, smaller architectures) and consider them as a practical constraint in deployment.
